title: API.
publishedHtml:
API is the system application programming interface for interacting with merchant platforms.

The interface is available at api.cloudpayments.ru and supports features for executing payments, canceling payments, issuing refunds, capturing two-stage payments, creating and canceling subscriptions for recurring payments, and sending invoices via email.

How it works

  • Parameters are sent via the POST method either as key=value pairs in the request body or in JSON format.

  • The API can accept no more than 150,000 fields per single request. API response timeout: 5 minutes.

  • In all requests to the API, if you pass a floating-point number into an integer field, the API does not return an error; instead, mathematical rounding will be applied automatically.

  • The API limits the maximum number of concurrent requests to 5 for test terminals and to 30 for production terminals. If the number of requests currently processed exceeds the limit, the API returns a 429 HTTP status code (Too Many Requests) until at least one request has finished processing. If you need to revise these limits, contact your account manager.

The choice of parameter transmission format is determined on the client side and controlled through the Content-Type request header.

  • For key=value parameters, use Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

  • For JSON parameters, use Content-Type: application/json.

The system returns a JSON response containing at least the following two parameters: Success and Message:

javascript
{ "Success": false, "Message": "Invalid Amount value" }

Request authentication

To authenticate a request, HTTP Basic Auth is used to send the username and password within the HTTP request header. The Public ID is used as the username, and the API Secret is used as the password. Both values can be obtained from the dashboard.

Warning: If the request does not include an authentication header or contains incorrect authentication data, the system returns a 401 HTTP status (Unauthorized).

Notice: The API Secret is used for security. It must be stored in a secure location.

API idempotency

Idempotency is an API property that ensures that a repeated request returns the same result as the initial request without being processed again. This means that you can send multiple requests to a system with the same ID, only one successful request will be processed, and all responses will be identical. This mechanism protects against network errors that could otherwise result in duplicate records or actions.

To enable idempotency, pass the X-Request-ID header containing a unique ID in your API request. You generate this request ID. It can be a GUID, a combination of the order number, date, and amount, or any other value at your discretion.

Each new request that requires processing must include a unique X-Request-ID value. The processed result is retained in the system for 1 hour.

Cryptogram payment

Notice: According to the NSPK requirements, merchant platforms providing telecommunication services (MCC 4814 Telecommunication Services), must provide the payer's phone number. If the phone number is missing from the request, acquiring banks will decline the transactions.

The phone number must be passed in the Phone parameter within the Payer object.

Format: digits only, without delimiters such as hyphens, or parentheses.

Example: "+71234567890"

Notice: The amount parameter does not accept transaction amounts less than 0.01.

The server returns a JSON file with the following three properties:

  • Success field: request result

  • Message field: error description

  • Model object: extended information

Possible responses:

  • Malformed request:

    • Success: false

    • Message: error description

  • Requires 3D Secure authentication:

    • Success: false

    • Model: authentication data

  • Transaction declined:

    • Success: false

    • Model: transaction information and an error code

  • Transaction accepted:

    • Success: true

    • Model: transaction information

Notice: The request result (the Success field) does not reflect the transaction status; it only indicates the success or failure of the API request. The transaction status is reflected in the additional Status field, and can also be obtained via received notifications. For the interpretation of transaction statuses, see reference.

Processing 3D Secure

To perform 3D Secure authentication you must redirect the payer to the address specified in the AcsUrl parameter of the server response, passing the following parameters:

  • MD: TransactionId parameters from the server response

  • PaReq: the parameter of the same name from the server response

  • TermUrl: the return URL on your website where the payer is redirected after authentication

Notice: Note that parameter names are case-sensitive.

Method for token payments using a token generated during a cryptogram payment or via a Pay notification.

Notice: A token payment can only be processed on the terminal (publicId) where the token was originally generated. If you need to share tokens across multiple terminals, send a free-form request to assistant@cp.ru.

Notice: The final status of an SBP token payment (Completed/Declined) can be obtained via the Pay and Fail notifications after the transaction has been created, rather than in the payment request response.

The server returns a JSON file with three components: the success field (the result of the request), the message field (a description of the error), and the model object (extended information).

Possible options

  • Malformed request:

    • Message: error description

  • Transaction declined:

    • Success: false

    • Model: transaction information and an error code

  • Transactions accepted:

    • Success: true

    • Model: transaction information
